exam.title: Exam #2 — Trigonometry
exam.notes: Covers chapters 3 and 4. Give exact answers unless a problem says to round: rationalize denominators and keep π in radian answers. The first problem is always on the unit circle.

units.summary: Reference angles, degrees and radians, arcs and sectors

units.title: The six functions and the unit circle
units.summary: Exact values, terminal points and inverse functions

skills.title: Reference angles and degrees-minutes
skills.summary: Find the reference angle of any angle and switch between decimal degrees and degrees-minutes-seconds.
objectives: Name the quadrant of an angle in standard position
Find the reference angle in each quadrant
Convert between decimal degrees and degrees-minutes-seconds

skills.title: Exact degree–radian conversion
skills.summary: Convert between degrees and radians exactly, keeping π in the answer.
objectives: Explain what one radian measures
Convert degrees to radians in simplest form
Convert radians to degrees

skills.title: Arc length & sector area applications
skills.summary: Use s = rθ and A = ½r²θ to solve problems about wheels, sprinklers and pendulums.
objectives: Find arc length and sector area with the angle in radians
Solve for the radius or the angle
Relate angular and linear speed

skills.title: Exact values of the six trig functions
skills.summary: Combine reference angles and quadrant signs with the special-angle table to find exact values without a calculator.
objectives: Recall the exact sine, cosine and tangent of 30°, 45° and 60°
Use the quadrant to choose the sign
Find csc, sec and cot exactly and rationalize

skills.title: Unit-circle coordinates and arc distance t
skills.summary: Find the terminal point P(t) on the unit circle for any real number t and read off sin t and cos t.
objectives: Find terminal points for the special values of t
Use reference numbers and quadrant signs
Use x² + y² = 1 to find a missing coordinate

skills.title: Finding angles with a calculator
skills.summary: Use the inverse trig keys in the right mode and find every angle that solves the equation.
objectives: Use sin⁻¹, cos⁻¹ and tan⁻¹ in degree and radian mode
Find all solutions in [0°, 360°)
Solve right-triangle angle problems

skills.title: Graphs of sine and cosine
skills.summary: Sketch y = sin x and y = cos x from their five key points and read period, range, zeros and symmetry.
objectives: Sketch one period of sine and cosine
Read zeros, maxima and minima
Use even/odd symmetry

skills.title: Amplitude, period & phase shift
skills.summary: Read and build sinusoids y = A sin(B(x − C)) + D from their graph features.
objectives: Read amplitude, period, phase shift and midline
Write an equation from its features
Model a periodic situation

blueprint.instructions: Show your work. Exact answers unless told to round.

glossary.definition: An angle whose vertex is at the origin and whose initial side lies on the positive x-axis.
The ray where an angle in standard position stops.
The acute angle θ′ between the terminal side of an angle and the x-axis.
Angles that share a terminal side; they differ by a multiple of 360° (or 2π).
One sixtieth of a degree: 1′ = (1/60)°.
The central angle that cuts off an arc as long as the radius; π radians = 180°.
The distance along a circle: s = rθ, with θ in radians.
The region bounded by two radii and the arc between them; its area is ½r²θ.
The angle turned per unit of time, ω = θ/t.
The distance traveled per unit of time by a point on a turning circle, v = rω.
The circle x² + y² = 1, centered at the origin with radius 1.
The point P(t) reached by traveling a distance t along the unit circle from (1, 0).
The shortest distance along the unit circle from P(t) to the x-axis.
A value written with integers, fractions, radicals and π, without rounding: −√3/2, not −0.866.
Rewrite a fraction so the denominator has no radical: 1/√3 = √3/3.
csc θ = 1/sin θ, sec θ = 1/cos θ and cot θ = 1/tan θ.
“All Students Take Calculus”: which functions are positive in Quadrants I, II, III and IV.
sin⁻¹ x, the angle in [−90°, 90°] whose sine is x.
The length of one complete cycle of a periodic function; 2π for sin x and cos x.
Half the distance between the maximum and the minimum of a sinusoid: |A|.
The horizontal slide C of y = A sin(B(x − C)) + D; to the right when C > 0.
The horizontal line y = D halfway between the maximum and the minimum.
